participants: Chris Klevan (sales manager, running the meeting)
summary: Standing sales team meeting run by Chris Klevan: wins round, weekly projections per rep, then a closer-only call review and role play. Chris announced that Harry Edmonds has left the team by mutual agreement, that marketing direction is being changed to target the profile that closes best, and that ad spend and lead flow are temporarily down. He instituted a new deposit policy on the spot — no onboarding or follow-up call goes on the calendar without a deposit, and if the prospect cannot move money, take a card on file instead. The back half was a call review of Ben Byrne's lost Ricardo call, where the objection was 'for $6,000 I could get somebody in person', followed by an extended role play on reframing personal-trainer comparisons and spouse objections back onto certainty and results. The meeting ends with Ben leaving to take the David Elder call, which is the other Ben Byrne transcript from this date.
notable: Chris Klevan told Ben he had looked up the prospect's personal financial data before the call: 'I looked up his financial data. He's got 10K credit, he's got 106K income, he's a total beginner, so he's in a good spot.' The prospect was David Elder — on the call an hour later Elder disclosed no income at all, no savings, no monthly surplus and an inability to cover his own mortgage. Both the practice and the accuracy of the data source are exposures.

New deposit policy stated as a rule: 'moving forward, no onboarding calls go on the calendar unless we take a deposit', extended to follow-up calls and spouse objections — 'Deposits, deposits, deposits.' The deposit is to be described to prospects as refundable.

Card-on-file instruction: 'even if they're like, I cannot run money, be like, cool, then we'll just take down the card on file and I won't run it until this day ... Because once the card's on file, we can technically just run it.'

Deliberate non-disclosure of the deposit amount as a test: 'I actually like to not tell them what the deposit is going to be and then see if they react terribly to it. And then I say, Hey dude, like I could have told you it was $1. Like what's going on?'

Financial qualification is being applied by country of origin: 'if they come from certain, like UAE is one of those countries where I probably wouldn't hard financially qualify too much. If somebody's coming from Egypt, yeah, I probably would ... give them a little bit of a harder FQ.'

A prospect (Manny) no-showed and gave written feedback that he felt pressured and that his feelings about his father were used against him. Andrew Musial: 'he didn't like at the end that he felt pushed and used the emotions about his father and so on. Yeah, so I technically burned him.' The coaching response addressed objection isolation, not the pressure itself.

An AI chatbot handles inbound prospect texts and reps read those threads — 'He messaged our AI bot that I already know everything from the first call' and 'he actually texted also our AI chat bot, and I didn't see that'. No disclosure of the automation to prospects is mentioned anywhere.

A results guarantee is taught as an objection rebuttal: 'we're literally guaranteeing it' and 'when it comes to guaranteeing the results, like we do'. The exact terms of the guarantee are never stated.

Chris stated an affordability policy that constrains payment plans: 'I only sell people if I know for sure they can afford it and it's not going to put them in a tight spot when I offer payment plans ... the only time I ever do something financially for somebody that I'm like, whoa, that's not something I would do, is if they suggest it. Because I'm not here to play God.'
Setters are instructed to send free resources to prospects who cannot afford anything ('completely FDQ'), framed as the team value 'leave people better than when you found them'.

Primal University is confirmed as a live commissionable downsell product at roughly $200/month — 'it turned out, like, $200 is a lot for him' and 'you could still potentially get them in Primal University, which you will get commissioned for'.

Personnel and pipeline context: Harry Edmonds has left the team; weekly pace at the time of the meeting was two units and $9k cash; Ben Byrne had a pending close (Jorge, Spain) awaiting an international transfer and had taken no deposit, which is what triggered the new policy.

Chris's coaching contains a genuine counter-pressure instruction that is worth preserving: he rejected Andrew's line 'you wouldn't be on this call if you could do it by yourself' as too strong, saying 'I do believe that people can do it on their own ... I always put them in an empowered state.' He also asked, on the spouse objection, 'would you saying yes to this, like, put you in the doghouse? ... I'm also not in the businesses of ruining marriages.'
